messages:
elaine_pm: Heads-up — we need to finalize the embeddings endpoint spec for next quarter. Focus: batching limits, dims, model selection, response shape, and launch criteria. Can we sync here?

jay_ml: +1. Key tradeoffs are latency vs cost. We should propose a default model and a fallback smaller one.

kate_infra: What's the expected QPS and max vectors per request? that'll drive autoscaler and GPU memory sizing.

elaine_pm: Customer asks so far: batch uploads up to ~10k vectors (SaaS migration), but most usage is 1-100 vectors. Propose tiered limits: 100 / 1k / 10k with different timeouts. Thoughts?

omar_api: Tiered makes sense. Implementation note: we shouldn't let a single request block the runtime. Suggest soft limit for synchronous path at 1k vectors; >1k should be async job with job_id + polling/webhook.

maria_ds: For model dims: many customers use 1536 (similar to other open models). We should support 768, 1536, and 3072 to cover small->large needs. Default 1536.

jay_ml: Agree on dims. Model selection: propose redwood-embed-1 (1536) as default; redwood-embed-lite (768) for cost-sensitive, redwood-embed-large (3072) for semantic heavy workloads. Also a quantized variant for Dedicated/Private.

ben_pm: Launch criteria idea: SDKs (+examples), server-side batching in runtime, docs + cost estimator, perf benchmark (p95 latency under X ms for 1-100 vectors), and async jobs for >1k. Also need canary in Dedicated.

omar_api: Response JSON shape proposal (single call for up to sync_limit):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-1",
  "usage": { "input_vectors": 3 },
  "data": [
    { "id": "v0", "embedding": [0.001, -0.23, ...], "metadata": {"source": "upload.csv"} },
    { "id": "v1", "embedding": [0.12, 0.03, ...], "metadata": {} }
  ]
}
```
Include id echoing and optional metadata. No base64; raw floats.

maria_ds: Raw floats will be large for big batches. Consider optional compressed output (gzip + base64) for async export job. For sync responses keep raw floats.

kate_infra: Memory checks: 1k vectors * 1536 dims * 4 bytes ~ 6MB raw but intermediate concat and kernels add overhead. 10k sync is unrealistic on hosted. Async only for >1k as mentioned.

jay_ml: Batching limits for runtime: internal batching window default 10ms, max combined tokens/vectors per batch cap we need to choose. Propose batch cap 16k vectors aggregated; will keep latency low and throughput high on GPU.

elaine_pm: Can we define SLOs tied to tiers? e.g., sync tier (<=100 vectors): p95 < 120ms, medium (101-1k): p95 < 500ms, async: worker SLA 1h for 10k jobs?

kate_infra: Those look reasonable. Need to validate on our infra queue model. Also request size limits for HTTP body: recommend clients upload larger payloads using multipart or presigned storage for >5MB.

omar_api: API surface decisions: keep /v1/embeddings for sync, /v1/embeddings/jobs for async (create + status + download). SDKs should expose auto-chunking and retry.

ben_pm: Prioritization — MVP (hosted API): default model, sync up to 100, async job for >100, docs, SDK support for auto-chunking, usage metrics. Phase 2: add 1k sync for enterprise + Dedicated + quantized models.

maria_ds: Eval plan: semantic search similarity A/B vs baseline on 5 customer corpora, vector quality thresholds (NDCG delta within 2% of baseline), and regression alerts on model upgrades.

elaine_pm: Launch checklist starter: API proto + spec, SDK patches, infra autoscale plan, perf harness results, pricing notes, and marketing one-pager. Who owns each?

omar_api: I'll own API proto + SDK hooks for auto-chunking.

kate_infra: I'll own autoscale and max batch config + presigned upload pattern.

jay_ml: I'll own model variants and perf harness. Maria can lead evals.

maria_ds: Yep, I'll set up the corpora and baseline tests.

ben_pm: I'll draft the launch criteria doc and coordinate with legal/pricing.

deploy_bot: Note: created task EMB-152 for async job API.

elaine_pm: Ok next step — Omar to post a compact API spec snippet and example SDK call by EOD Thursday. Add explicit limit numbers in that post so infra can simulate. @kate_infra @jay_ml @maria_ds please review then. :rocket:
